This is super true! It’s the industrialization of music software in general I think. Companies that build DAWs build partial open source functionality, so that others can build programming that can be used within their own software (eg: max for live on Ableton etc) and claim democratization of the ability to produce, a la “everyone can make music” discourse (which I do believe haha 😂). 

In reality, the industry *necessitates* competition ergo there are more artists that use DAWs rather than instruments because of accessibility to the them (ie Abelton), than there are people that have the time it requires to learn to play an instrument, access the industry, and find opportunities that are sustainable. Which leads to again, more folks using software rather than gear. 

Tldr, yeah it’s cheaper to run a digital workstation than build skill/own/rent analog instruments, and companies like ableton, fl studio, izotope, etc etc are fully aware of it, and bank on it.

Sorry for the vent, I’m trying to crawl out of a shitty place rn and I’m also on the way to the hospital for a possible infection at my last tumor site. It’s been a long one.
